correctness.rationale: Maximal-point coloring criterion: onto p-morphism to a k-fork exists iff the color set above every world is either singleton or all k colors and some world sees all k. If x has >=2 active non-top coordinates in P_bm, for each pair of maximal extensions from distinct coordinate groups a witness w>=x with exactly those two maxima forces their colors equal when k>=3. Consequently all maxima above x monochromatic. If x has one active coordinate, at most b maxima above it, prohibiting a k-root for k>max(b,2). The root preimage in any generated subframe has principal upset included, and its image still surjects by back lifting. Sharpness: P_b,1=H_b for b>=2; P_1,2 onto H_2. Coordinatewise surjections D_c→D_b preserving unique preimage of top induce p-morphisms P_c,m→P_b,m, giving inclusion; characteristic formulas chi(H_c) establish strictness. We independently enumerated maximal-color configurations in principal generated upsets of P_b,m for 1<=b,m<=3 and k<=4; these tests include generated subframes rather than just whole P_b,m, a necessary distinction, and agreed with all cutoffs.
